title: Layout, safety and how much your workshop can make

say: Layout, safety, and how much your workshop can make.
This is the video for module two of Factory and Workshop Setup.
In this module your space becomes a working system. First, a floor plan designed around how the product moves, not where the furniture fits.

panel.heading: Turn your space into a working system
items: Know your ceiling and your floor

say: Second, a simple written risk assessment for fire, electricity, fumes, chemicals and first aid.

panel.heading: Turn your space into a working system
items: Know your ceiling and your floor

say: Third, two numbers: the most your workshop can make, and the least it must sell to pay for itself.

panel.heading: Turn your space into a working system
items: Know your ceiling and your floor

say: Write your process as stages. Each stage becomes a zone, placed in order, so work flows one way instead of criss-crossing.
Receiving goes near the door, so heavy sacks are not carried through the work.

panel.heading: Zones in the order the product moves
items: Receive and store materials, near the door

say: Put dusty, hot or smelly work near a window with a fan blowing out. Place machines near sockets so no cable crosses a walkway.

panel.heading: Zones in the order the product moves
items: Receive and store materials, near the door

say: Keep raw materials and finished goods apart, and keep one clear walkway to the exit.
A common mistake is storing finished goods in the walkway just for today. It becomes permanent and blocks the exit.

panel.heading: Zones in the order the product moves
items: Receive and store materials, near the door

say: In a straight-line flow, materials enter at one end and leave at the other. It suits long rooms with two doors.

panel.heading: Straight line or U-shape?
left: In at one end, out at the other
right: One person can help two stations

say: In a U-shape, work goes down one side and back up the other. For example, Hauwa in Kano has a 24 square metre room with one door, so she chose a U-shape.
Draw your plan to scale, then mark the zones on the real floor with tape and run one batch before you pay a carpenter.

left: In at one end, out at the other
right: One person can help two stations

say: A hazard is anything that could cause harm. Risk is how likely harm is, and how bad. Walk your workshop with a notebook.

panel.heading: Find hazards, score them, act
items: Walk the workshop and list the hazards

say: Score likelihood and severity from 1 to 3 and multiply. A score of 6 or 9 needs action now. 3 or 4 needs action soon.

panel.heading: Find hazards, score them, act
items: Walk the workshop and list the hazards

say: For example, Kemi in Ibadan found lacquer thinner beside a hot plate. That scored 9. She moved the thinner to a closed metal cabinet and replaced the hot plate with a glue method that needs no flame.

panel.heading: Find hazards, score them, act
items: Walk the workshop and list the hazards

say: Work from the top of the hierarchy of control. Eliminate, then substitute, then engineer, then rules and training. Protective equipment comes last.

panel.heading: Find hazards, score them, act
items: Walk the workshop and list the hazards
panel.rule: Remove a hazard first. Protective equipment is the last line.

say: Fire needs heat, fuel and oxygen. Rags, sawdust and packaging are fuel. Keep flammables away from heat, and keep the extinguisher near the exit.
Never use water on an electrical fire or burning oil. The emergency number in Nigeria is 112.

cards.d: Never use water on electrical or oil fires. Extinguisher by the exit. Post 112 by the door.
Fan blowing out. Original labelled containers, stored low. Keep bleach and acids apart.
A named first aider and a stocked kit. Anything beyond minor cuts goes to a clinic.

say: Work with fumes and dust near an open window with a fan blowing out. Keep every chemical in its labelled original container, never a drink bottle, and keep acids and bleach apart.

cards.d: Never use water on electrical or oil fires. Extinguisher by the exit. Post 112 by the door.
Fan blowing out. Original labelled containers, stored low. Keep bleach and acids apart.
A named first aider and a stocked kit. Anything beyond minor cuts goes to a clinic.

say: Name one person in charge of first aid and keep a stocked kit where everyone can reach it. Write every incident or near miss in a log.

say: Time each stage with a phone stopwatch. If two machines do the same job, divide by two. Hauwa sews a bag in 30 minutes on each of two machines, so 15 minutes a bag.

panel.heading: Find the bottleneck and your capacity
items: Time each stage for one unit
Divide by parallel machines or workers

say: Sewing is her longest stage, so it is the bottleneck.

panel.heading: Find the bottleneck and your capacity
items: Time each stage for one unit
Divide by parallel machines or workers

say: Her day has 420 working minutes. Machines are not productive every minute, so she plans at 80 percent: 336 minutes. That gives 22 bags a day, or 528 bags a month.
Speeding up cutting changes nothing. She needs more sewing time.

panel.heading: Find the bottleneck and your capacity
items: Time each stage for one unit
Divide by parallel machines or workers
panel.rule: The whole workshop can only go as fast as its bottleneck.

say: Running costs come every month, whether you produce or not. Keep them separate from one-time setup costs.
Hauwa pays rent, power and fuel, water and cleaning, two machinists and maintenance.

That is about 280,000 naira a month. Each bag leaves 3,000 naira after materials and packaging. 280,000 divided by 3,000 means she must sell 94 bags a month just to cover the workshop. She sells about 450, so the space is paying for itself.

To remember. Zones follow the product. Score hazards and fix the worst first. No water on electrical or oil fires. The bottleneck sets your capacity. And divide running costs by what each unit contributes to find your break-even.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Zones follow the product, one way through
Score hazards and fix the highest first
No water on electrical or oil fires

say: Your tasks: draw your zoned floor plan and test it with tape, write your scored risk assessment, and calculate your capacity and break-even.
